title: The Second Start of Onsi Sawiris, Years After Egypt Took His Firm
conflicts: Orascom founding year: 1975 (Daily News Egypt), 1976 (Egypt Independent, Xinhua, Family Business Histories), 1977 (International Directory of Company Histories); story gives all three. Staff at restart: five (IDCH) vs three in 'two rooms and a hall' (Coptic Orthodox Cultural Center); story gives both with sources. Sawiris's own 'twelve years in Libya' from 1966 implies about 1978, later than the founding dates; story attributes the twelve years to him and dates the return to the mid-1970s. IDCH ties the return to Camp David, which it misdates to 1976 (signed 1978); that link is not used. Role after nationalisation: 'head' / 'executive manager' vs 'forced to work as an employee'; story says he stayed on to run it for the state. Age at death 90 vs 91; story uses 90.
notes: Mostly obituaries plus a reference-book company history; founder voice comes from a television interview quoted by The National and words quoted by the Coptic Orthodox Cultural Center. The repeat screen flagged tabitha-karanja-keroche-kra-tax-demand-2006 but passed it (different founder and episode). Stance: affirms.
